basis:
WHAT THIS FILE IS. The envelope the speed gate judges: per population, each entry's recorded statement count, its wall smoke envelope, and the `seeds` list that declares which entry ids may be seeded. `interpreter` names the CPython MAJOR.MINOR the counts were measured on.

WHAT FAILED FIVE TIMES, AND WHY THE INSTRUMENT CHANGED. Five instances red main on unchanged code (#190, #216, #221, #240 and #269), because every CPU-derived quantity follows the runner: raw CPU seconds carried a 1.96x machine factor on identical code, and no scalar calibration cancels a heterogeneous pool. Issue #269 is the measured proof: at 447e92f the unit-suite net value read 31.59 against a committed max of 22.0354 (+43.4% over the +30% budget) while its calibration child read ~65% higher than the baseline cell's runner, and the pool had moved to ubuntu-26.04 while the baseline `cell` names ubuntu-24.04. Between the two #269 runs d(raw)/d(calibration) measured about 30.1 against the committed slope 21.3716 — the net value still scales with the machine factor whenever the slope is not exactly the local ratio, so the calibrated instrument is retired, and with it the gates it kept red.

THE INSTRUMENT IS A DETERMINISTIC STATEMENT COUNT. The measured child counts its own sys.monitoring LINE events (Python 3.12+; the speed job pins 3.15): same code plus same collected population gives the same executed lines and the same count, on any runner, under any load. Measured on the box that shipped the instrument (2026-10-26, CPython 3.13, tree 5c3b9d6, env pinned per counter.child_environment): 99,222,446 / 99,222,443 / 99,220,993 events over three runs — spread 0.0015% — missed: 0 every run, suite exit 0 every run.

WHAT THE COUNT DOES NOT SEE. The count covers the direct child's own executed lines. Nested Python children and non-Python subprocesses — the renderers' git calls — are not counted. A commit that moved all of a renderer's work into git would show its entry flat: that is what the wall smoke bound is for, and it is why the renderer/git side of this gate is measured by the wall smoke bound only until the seeded statement counts stand. Not a wall or CPU quantity, so neither load nor the machine factor reaches it.

WHY TOLERANCE 0.05. The observed three-run spread of the instrument is 0.0015%; 0.05 is thousands-fold headroom and still far below any real step change, so an ordinary run passes by orders of magnitude and a doubled program cannot. The envelopes this file records stay min/max/n envelopes: once the seeds land, each entry's record is the folded head value as both bounds with n equal to the seeding run's report count, and from there the down-only ratchet and the (1 + tolerance) ceiling apply unchanged.

WHAT MAIN'S FIRST PUSH SEEDS. The ratchet writer seeds every seed-declared entry from the first passing default-branch push: the folded head value as both bounds, n equal to the report count, and the step derives the removals the reset needs through the head document's seeds lists (recorded at the base, seed-declared in the head, no longer recorded). wall never seeds. The renderer listing loop, the raise derivation and everything else in the ratchet step is unchanged.

THE PYTHON 3.15 RE-SEED (issue #262). Moving the speed job from CPython 3.13 to 3.15 changes how many lines a workload executes, so every entry was re-seeded from one 3.15 run, through the interpreter-move route: renderer raises are admitted only because base and head `interpreter` differ, and the move is their only reason. Same-tree pair, two rounds each, folded per-run minimum as both bounds, n = 2. 3.13: PR #349 head 2e50062, tests run 43195584228. 3.15: PR #349 head ce0d8e2, tests run 43198074100. e2e::bench.render 108578 -> 104426 (3.13: 109020 / 109097; 3.15: 104505 / 104426), lowered. e2e::bench.render-impact 701427 -> 716278 (3.13: 703036 / 703001; 3.15: 716317 / 716278), raised by the move. e2e::bench.render-responsiveness 93463 -> 106894 (3.13: 93911 / 93911; 3.15: 106894 / 106894), raised by the move. counter::unit-suite 99873148 -> 79559531 (3.15: 79559531 / 79559808), lowered; its 3.13 run (80316927 / 80318381) collected three fewer tests than the 3.15 one, which adds the route's own pins. On 3.13 every renderer workload still fit its previous ceiling (x 1.05), so the two raises belong to the interpreter, not the tree.

PROVENANCE. measured_commit names ce0d8e2, the tree the 3.15 run above measured (the re-seed commit after it changes this document only); the three instrument runs above measured 5c3b9d6; the unit-suite `population` digest is collected from the tree this document commits and the renderer digest from e2e_bench.py --list-workloads, both by the documented commands. The `wall` envelopes are byte-identical to the previous record, observed on 3.13; the 3.15 runs passed the smoke bound against them, and wall maxima stay down-only across an interpreter move. `cell` no longer describes the gated value — the statement count is runner-independent by construction — so it records only where the wall envelopes were observed.
cell: the wall envelopes below were observed on ubuntu-latest GitHub-hosted runners (image ubuntu-24.04/20261012.334.1 and earlier 20260927.320); the gated statement count is runner-independent
